blocks.text: 45 תְּפִלָּה לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה 45
uncertainties: This is the running header, not prayer text. The vowels follow the printed head as far as I could read them.

blocks.text: וּבְכֵן תֵּן פַּחְדְּךָ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ עַל כָּל־מַעֲשֶׂיךָ וְאֵימָתְךָ עַל כָּל־מַה־שֶּׁבָּרָאתָ וְיִירָאוּךָ כָּל־הַמַּעֲשִׂים וְיִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לְפָנֶיךָ כָּל־הַבְּרוּאִים וְיֵעָשׂוּ כֻלָּם אֲגֻדָּה אַחַת לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנְךָ בְּלֵבָב שָׁלֵם כְּמוֹ שֶׁיָּדַעְנוּ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ שֶׁהַשָּׁלְטָן לְפָנֶיךָ עֹז בְּיָדְךָ וּגְבוּרָה בִּימִינֶךָ וְשִׁמְךָ נוֹרָא עַל כָּל־מַה־שֶּׁבָּרָאתָ׃
uncertainties: Throughout the page, this typeface draws the qamats of final kaf (ךָ) inside the letter, so ךָ and ךְ are hard to tell apart. I read ךָ for the 2nd-person suffixes (פַּחְדְּךָ, וְאֵימָתְךָ, רְצוֹנְךָ, בְּיָדְךָ, וְשִׁמְךָ). Please check against the image.
Line breaks fall after כָּל־ at the ends of lines 1 and 2. The maqaf is printed at the line end, and each line break has been rejoined.
The holam on עֹז (over ע/ז) is faint.

blocks.text: וּבְכֵן תֵּן כָּבוֹד יְיָ לְעַמֶּךָ תְּהִלָּה לִירֵאֶיךָ וְתִקְוָה לְדוֹרְשֶׁיךָ וּפִתְחוֹן פֶּה לַמְיַחֲלִים לָךְ שִׂמְחָה לְאַרְצֶךָ וְשָׂשׂוֹן לְעִירֶךָ וּצְמִיחַת קֶרֶן לְדָוִד עַבְדֶּךָ וַעֲרִיכַת נֵר לְבֶן־יִשַׁי מְשִׁיחֶךָ בִּמְהֵרָה בְיָמֵינוּ׃
uncertainties: בְיָמֵינוּ: I can't tell whether the ב has a dagesh (בְּ or בְ).
לַמְיַחֲלִים: the patah under ל and the sheva under מ are small and close together.
יִשַׁי: I see no dagesh in the ש.

blocks.text: וּבְכֵן צַדִּיקִים יִרְאוּ וְיִשְׂמָחוּ וִישָׁרִים יַעֲלֹזוּ וַחֲסִידִים בְּרִנָּה יָגִילוּ וְעוֹלָתָה תִּקְפָּץ־פִּיהָ. וְכָל־הָרִשְׁעָה כֻּלָּהּ כְּעָשָׁן תִּכְלֶה כִּי תַעֲבִיר מֶמְשֶׁלֶת זָדוֹן מִן־הָאָרֶץ׃
uncertainties: כֻּלָּהּ: I can't tell whether the final ה has a mappiq.
תִּכְלֶה: the vowel under ל could be segol or qamats. The full page looks like segol.

blocks.text: וְתִמְלוֹךְ אַתָּה יְיָ לְבַדֶּךָ עַל כָּל־מַעֲשֶׂיךָ בְּהַר צִיּוֹן מִשְׁכַּן כְּבוֹדֶךָ וּבִירוּשָׁלַיִם עִיר קָדְשֶׁךָ. כַּכָּתוּב בְּדִבְרֵי קָדְשֶׁךָ
uncertainties: Here ירושלים is written plene with the yod (וּבִירוּשָׁלַיִם), which is how it looks in the image.

blocks.text: יִמְלֹךְ יְהֹוָה לְעוֹלָם אֱלֹהַיִךְ צִיּוֹן לְדֹר וָדֹר הַלְלוּיָהּ׃
uncertainties: The source is Psalm 146:10. The page does not print a reference.

Cantillation: I couldn't reliably make out any taamim at this resolution. There may be small marks, for example on יִמְלֹךְ and הַלְלוּיָהּ, and an apparent meteg on ה of הַלְלוּיָהּ. I left them out rather than guess.
The vowel on the divine name (יְהֹוָה or יְהוָֹה) is uncertain.
לְעוֹלָם is printed plene here, unlike the Masoretic defective לְעֹלָם. Keep it as printed.
הַלְלוּיָהּ: the mappiq in the final ה is probable but small.

blocks.text: קָדוֹשׁ אַתָּה וְנוֹרָא שְׁמֶךָ וְאֵין אֱלוֹהַּ מִבַּלְעָדֶיךָ. כַּכָּתוּב
uncertainties: אֱלוֹהַּ: the dot in the final ה (mappiq) is probable.

blocks.text: וַיִּגְבַּהּ יְיָ צְבָאוֹת בַּמִּשְׁפָּט וְהָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ נִקְדַּשׁ בִּצְדָקָה.
uncertainties: The source is Isaiah 5:16. The page does not print a reference. It prints יְיָ, not the Tetragrammaton.
Cantillation: there is a mark under the ו of וַיִּגְבַּהּ, possibly a patah plus a ga'ya or meteg. I couldn't confirm any other taamim.
וַיִּגְבַּהּ: the mappiq in the final ה is probable.
The verse ends with a period, not a sof pasuq.

blocks.text: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ הַמֶּלֶךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ׃

אַתָּה בְחַרְתָּנוּ מִכָּל הָעַמִּים. אָהַבְתָּ אוֹתָנוּ וְרָצִיתָ בָּנוּ. וְרוֹמַמְתָּנוּ מִכָּל הַלְּשׁוֹנוֹת. וְקִדַּשְׁתָּנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתֶיךָ. וְקֵרַבְתָּנוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ לַעֲבוֹדָתֶךָ. וְשִׁמְךָ הַגָּדוֹל וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ עָלֵינוּ קָרָאתָ׃
uncertainties: בְחַרְתָּנוּ: I can't tell whether the ב has a dagesh.
בְּמִצְוֹתֶיךָ: the holam is placed on the vav (מִצְוֹתֶיךָ). This needs a check.

blocks.text: וַתִּתֶּן־לָנוּ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ בְּאַהֲבָה אֶת־יוֹם (הַשַּׁבָּת הַזֶּה וְאֶת יוֹם) הַזִּכָּרוֹן הַזֶּה. יוֹם (זִכְרוֹן) תְּרוּעָה (בְּאַהֲבָה) מִקְרָא קֹדֶשׁ זֵכֶר לִיצִיאַת מִצְרָיִם׃
uncertainties: The three parenthetical insertions are set in smaller type. See the Shabbat alternatives in notes.

blocks.text: 45 Morning Prayer for the New Year 45
ובכן

And therefore put the fear of Thee, O Lord our God, upon all Thy works and awe of Thee upon all that Thou hast created, so that all works may fear Thee and all the created bow down before Thee and all of them may be made into one group for the performance of Thy will with a complete heart, since we know, O Lord our God, that dominion lies before Thee, that strength is in Thy hand and might in Thy right hand and that Thy Name inspires with awe all that Thou has created.
uncertainties: "Thou has created." is printed exactly like this. See correction candidates.

blocks.text: ובכן

And therefore grant honour, O Lord, to Thy people, fame to those who fear Thee and praise to those who seek Thee and confidence to those who wait for Thee, joy to Thy land happiness to Thy city and a rise of fortune to David Thy servant and an array of light to the son of Jesse Thine anointed speedily and in our days.
uncertainties: There is no comma after "land". That is how it is printed.

blocks.text: ובכן

And thus may the righteous see and rejoice and the upright exult and the pious revel with joy. Vice shall close its mouth and all evil entirely disappear like smoke when Thou removest the dominion of arrogance from the earth.
ותמלוך
And Thou, O Lord, shalt reign alone over all Thy works on Mount Zion, Thy glorious dwelling, and in Jerusalem, Thy Holy City, as it is written in Thy holy word,
uncertainties: "Jeru-/salem" is a line-break hyphen and has been rejoined.
I split the English at the start of the verse to match the Hebrew. On the page it is one paragraph.

blocks.text: the Lord shall reign for ever, your God, O Zion, from generation to generation. Halleluyah!
uncertainties: The "L" in "Lord" (first line of this paragraph) has a printing artifact (it looks like "L.ord"). The intended word is Lord.

blocks.text: קדוש
Holy art Thou and awe-inspiring is Thy Name and there is no God beside Thee, as it is written,
uncertainties: "awe-inspiring" has a real (lexical) hyphen.

blocks.text: exalted is the Lord of Hosts through judgment and the Holy God is sanctified through righteousness.
Blessed art Thou, O Lord, the Holy King.
אתה בחרתנו

Thou hast chosen us from all peoples, loved us and found delight in us and exalted us above all tongues and sanctified us through Thy commandments, and brought us near, O our King, to Thy service and proclaimed Thy great and holy Name unto us.
ותתן־לנו
uncertainties: The connector is printed like a hyphen or maqaf (ותתן-לנו). I recorded it as a maqaf.

blocks.text: Thou hast given us, O Lord our God, in love this day (of the Sabbath and this day) of remembrance, a day (of remembrance) of Teruah (in love) for a sacred convocation, a reminder of the exodus from Egypt.
uncertainties: "convoca-/tion" is a line-break hyphen and has been rejoined.

notes: These two scans have no Rashi-script rubrics and no speaker sigla.
Biblical citations have no printed references. They are Psalm 146:10 (s118 vetimlokh_cite) and Isaiah 5:16 (s118 kadosh_cite).

Shabbat alternatives in Hebrew (s118 vatiten_lanu), all in parentheses and smaller type: (1) 'הַשַּׁבָּת הַזֶּה וְאֶת יוֹם' between 'אֶת־יוֹם' and 'הַזִּכָּרוֹן'; (2) 'זִכְרוֹן' between 'יוֹם' and 'תְּרוּעָה'; (3) 'בְּאַהֲבָה' between 'תְּרוּעָה' and 'מִקְרָא'. Keep the inner text on Shabbat and drop it on a weekday. Either way, suppress the parentheses.

Shabbat alternatives in English (s119 vatiten_lanu): (1) 'of the Sabbath and this day' after 'this day'; (2) 'of remembrance' after 'a day'; (3) 'in love' after 'Teruah'. The brackets should be suppressed the same way. On a weekday the result reads 'this day of remembrance, a day of Teruah for a sacred convocation'.
Page continuation: Hebrew s118 ends at 'לִיצִיאַת מִצְרָיִם׃' and English s119 ends at 'exodus from Egypt.' Both are complete paragraph ends, and the next paragraph begins on the following scan.
Correction candidate: s119 uvkhen_ten_pachdekha has 'all that Thou has created.' The likely intended form is 'hast created', matching 'Thou hast created' earlier in the same paragraph.
Correction candidate: s119 uvkhen_ten_kavod has 'joy to Thy land happiness to Thy city'. A comma after 'land' is probably missing.

The Hebrew vowels are as seen at band resolution. Cantillation on the two citation verses could not be confirmed and is left out, not invented. A higher-resolution check is recommended for the taamim and mappiqs listed in the uncertainties.
